pr.title: Install each version under `~/.local/share/trip` without `sudo`, and switch to it only once it builds
pr.head: 4b41a6106f0cb2cff25e2394348b3554079daf40

summary: install.sh is how you put trip on a machine. Before this change it built whatever a checkout held and copied the binary to /usr/local/bin/trip with sudo. The machines that run trip use ~/.local/bin/trip instead, and a failed or interrupted install left nothing to fall back on.

This pull request is step 2 of the releases plan. The installer now builds each version into its own directory under ~/.local/share/trip/, without sudo, and switches to it only once the whole build succeeds. A failed build leaves the version you had in place and tells you which version did not install.

ModeHow you run itWhat it installs
Releasecurl … | bash, with no checkout beside the scriptThe source archive of TRIP_REF (default v0) from TRIP_REPO, built with TRIP_RELEASE=1 in a temporary directory
Checkout./install.sh in a cloneThe checkout, built where cargo builds it, installed as <version>-dev in the same layout
Linked./install.sh --dev in a cloneNo copy: ~/.local/bin/trip links to the checkout's debug build

In every mode the installer then adds the shell hook to ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc. The hook now runs trip env only when command -v trip finds trip. The installer also warns when ~/.local/bin is not on PATH or an old /usr/local/bin/trip remains, and prints the line that fixes each without running it.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Version directory: ~/.local/share/trip/<version>/, holding one build's trip binary.
  • current: a symlink naming the version directory that ~/.local/bin/trip runs, through current/trip.
  • previous: a symlink naming the version current named before the last switch, kept so you can switch back.
  • Daemon record: ~/.trip/daemon.json, the version and pid of a running daemon. A later step of the plan makes the daemon write it.
  • TRIP_RELEASE: a compile-time variable. Only a build with TRIP_RELEASE=1 reports a bare version instead of <version>-dev.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first Projector review, of ec8cdb3, requested changes with two findings and listed three suggestions. Since then, the branch was rebased onto #27's new head and gained five commits:

  • The release mode checks that the archive's Cargo.toml names trip, so another repository's archive fails with the installer's own message. This fixes the first finding.
  • test_shell_hook checks the old and the guarded hook in two straight runs. This fixes the second finding.
  • current and previous are read by their last path component, a hook with no closing fi is left alone with a warning, and cargo metadata names the checkout's target directory. These take up the three suggestions.

The review of this head settled both findings as fixed.

groups.title: The installer
groups.kicker: Three modes, a versioned layout, and a switch that happens only after a successful build
intro: The script picks its mode first. It treats the directory beside it as a checkout only when that directory's Cargo.toml names the package trip. So a copy downloaded on its own, as curl … | bash or a later trip upgrade runs it, takes the release mode. Everything above the last line only defines functions, so bash has read the whole script from curl before any of it runs.

Every mode that copies a binary ends in install_version. It asks the built binary for its version, copies it into a staging directory, and renames that into place. Then it switches previous, current, and ~/.local/bin/trip, each with one rename, so a running daemon keeps the file it already has open. Last, it deletes old versions, keeping the current one, the previous one, and the one a live daemon record names.

files.note: Rewritten from sh to bash with set -euo pipefail. Read install_version for the switch and pruning, install_release and install_checkout for the builds, target_dir for where a checkout build lands, and remove_hook for how an old hook is replaced.

checks.text: link_version returns a link's last path component. The installer writes bare version names, but a link someone switched back by hand, such as ln -sfn ~/.local/share/trip/0.2.0 current, holds an absolute path. Reading only the name keeps that version from being pruned.

On macOS, mv -T is refused as an illegal option, and the mv -h fallback replaced a symlink to a directory in place, without moving the new link into the old target. Checked by hand in a scratch directory.

The pruning loop deletes only real directories under ~/.local/share/trip whose names start with a digit. The version pattern above rejects / and a leading non-digit, so a version name cannot reach outside that directory.
tar extracts any repository's archive, so this check is what tells a TRIP_REPO typo apart from trip's source. Without it, a missing Cargo.toml stopped the script with a bare sed error.

With cargo 1.100, cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps prints one line of JSON with a single "target_directory": key, beside a separate build_directory, and this sed expression extracted exactly that path. Checked by running it in a checkout of this head.

The END rule makes awk exit 1 when a marker has no closing fi, so remove_hook returns before it writes the file. Run here, an edited hook gave status 1, and an intact one gave status 0 with the lines around it kept.

groups.title: The end-to-end test
groups.kicker: Each case runs the real installer in its own temporary HOME
intro: tests/install_e2e.py gives each case a fresh HOME and TMPDIR and a PATH of only cargo's directory and the system's, passed as a complete environment. Most cases install a stand-in crate named trip from local file:// archives, so they need no network and build in about a second. One case builds trip's own source, to show that a release build reports a bare version. check.yml already runs every tests/*_e2e.py, so CI picks it up.

files.note: Fourteen cases: a failed build, an archive that is not trip, pruning, a hand-made absolute current link, the daemon record (live and stale), the warnings, the shell hook, an edited hook, both checkout modes, a configured target-dir, no cargo, and a release build of trip itself.

checks.text: The environment each case passes the installer is complete, not merged with the caller's, so no real HOME, XDG variable, or PATH entry reaches it.

groups.title: README and plan
groups.kicker: The install instructions and what implementation settled
intro: The README gives the release command, which works once the first release is tagged, the checkout and --dev modes, the layout, and a terminal setup that names ~/.local/bin/trip enter. The plan adds the previous link to its layout table in § 2.2 and records the decisions this step settled in § 9.

files.note: The install section, the layout table, and the terminal setup now name ~/.local.

§ 2.2 gains previous. § 9 records the build time, the test-only variables, and that a checkout install builds in the checkout's own target directory, which § 2.3 step 2 still describes as a temporary directory.

checks.text: The plan stays in-progress. This change adds no open question, and the questions in § 7 are all deferred or owned.
